key_insight: vid2vid-long uses explicit correspondences across video frames to help preserve visual consistency over time. The key idea is to connect relevant frames rather than rely solely on a fixed-length window of recent history.
problem_solved: Fast video-to-video models often use limited causal attention windows, losing access to older visual information needed for long-range temporal consistency.
method: Introduce a correspondence-based approach called vid2vid-long for video-to-video translation.
Use explicit cross-frame relationships to connect relevant visual information across time.
Address consistency failures when useful history falls outside a model’s recent-frame context window.
impact: This approach targets a central challenge in interactive video generation: maintaining stable visuals without sacrificing responsiveness. The supplied abstract is truncated, so specific implementation details and measured speed or quality gains are not available.
visual_elements: Timeline showing useful historical frames falling outside a fixed attention window.
Cross-frame correspondence diagram linking the same object across distant frames.
Conceptual comparison of appearance drift versus temporally consistent translation.
Simple input-video → correspondence-guided translation → output-video pipeline.
paper_title: Consistent Video-to-Video Translation via Explicit Correspondences
paper_authors: Gaurav Parmar, Zhengqi Li, Richard Zhang, Jun-Yan Zhu, Srinivasa Narasimhan
